summary: Frontend-only test of interactive PropertyLifecycle timeline + LifecycleJourney cinematic scenes + SceneStats count-up badges on FOXY PROPERTY homepage. All 7 requested feature checks PASS. No console errors.

verification_details.homepage_load: PASS - / loads on 1440x900, 0 console errors, smooth scroll through hero->west->interior->propertylab->lifecycle-journey scenes->PropertyLifecycle->editorial->finale with no black gaps.

verification_details.cta_href_per_stage: PASS - lifecycle-cta href changes per stage exactly as spec (acquire/finance/let/manage -> /properties, /mortgages, /lettings, /property-management).
verification_details.auto_advance_and_pause_on_hover: PASS - with mouse moved outside section, stage auto-advanced from 'Structure the right funding' (finance) -> 'Bring it to market' (let) at t~6s. Progress ring stroke-dashoffset animated 136.96 -> 112.47 -> 88.39 -> 64.31 -> 39.82 -> 15.74 across t=0..5s, confirming 6s DURATION and requestAnimationFrame tick. When section is hovered (paused=true) the ring SVG is not rendered and stage does not advance (verified in earlier hover pass).

critical_code_review_comments: PropertyLifecycle uses useState<number>(0) for rafRef but requestAnimationFrame returns a number - fine; still consider guarding against double-fire in React 18 StrictMode (dev only) by tracking a mounted flag. Not a bug in prod build.

SceneStats CountUp animates from 0 to `to` but for the manage scene stat 'PROPERTY INSPECTIONS' the value 4 is very small — count-up over 1300ms is barely perceptible; acceptable but could gate short values with a shorter duration for consistency.
PropertyLifecycle CTA is an anchor with class hover:bg-[#e6c84f]; no data-testid variation per-stage — fine since it's aria/label-driven, but ensure analytics tracks selected stage on click.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To validate auto-advance reliably, dispatch mouseleave on [data-testid=home-lifecycle] after any programmatic scroll/click (scroll_into_view_if_needed and Playwright click both move the mouse into the section, triggering paused=true). Then poll [data-testid=lifecycle-detail] h3 textContent over ~7s; expect it to change (DURATION=6000ms).
